summary:
A.R.E.S. is a layered, integrated map and planner for a Mars astronaut on a single Marswalk in Jezero Crater. It combines optical (MRO HiRISE), topographic (USGS HiRISE slope data), spectral (CRISM-style mineral targets), and radiation layers in one view, filling the hyperlocal gap left by regional tools like Mars Trek.

Safety comes first. Ground steeper than 15° is blocked, and an A* pathfinder routes around it. A live EVA walk tracks oxygen, warns before the point of no return, and reroutes the astronaut during a simulated solar flare or suit-oxygen drop. A helmet-visor HUD and Perseverance point-of-view images show what the crew will see, while a Science Operations deck supports sampling and route comparison. Real NASA/USGS data is clearly separated from labeled simulation.
details:
A.R.E.S. Tactical EVA Navigator is a layered map, safety planner, and field-science tool for a Mars astronaut on a spacewalk, built around Jezero Crater. It gives a hyperlocal view of a 1 km square around one Marswalk, which global tools like Mars Trek don’t provide.

1. Safe traversal

  • Layers several NASA data types (optical, topographic, spectral, radiation) on one map, with an opacity slider.
  • The red no-go areas are real: slopes over 15°, computed from the USGS HiRISE terrain model of Jezero.
  • An A* pathfinder plans routes around those slopes. It estimates simulated oxygen use out and back, and gives a GO / CAUTION / NO-GO decision with a safety reserve.
  • A live EVA walk burns O₂ as the astronaut moves and warns “approaching point of no return” and “turn back now” before the reserve is lost.
  • Solar-flare and oxygen-drop emergencies reroute the astronaut from their current position to the nearest valid shelter or oxygen source, even mid-walk.

2. Science Operations deck

  • Field science and sample logger: at each waypoint the astronaut can drill core (science targets only) or scoop regolith. A 10-tube sample bar and a live payload mass track what is collected. Virtual instruments (SHERLOC, PIXL, SuperCam) produce scans, and every action adds simulated EVA minutes to a science time budget. Field notes and a sample manifest persist across page reloads. Science actions lock during a solar flare or oxygen emergency.
  • Spectral signature analyzer: shows a reflectance spectrum (1.0–2.6 µm) for the selected waypoint, with hoverable absorption bands (for example, 2.21 µm for hydrated silica and the 2.30/2.50 µm carbonate pair). It also shows mineral percentages and splits the biosignature priority into aqueous alteration, organic preservation, context value, and access/safety, so judges see why a target ranks where it does.
  • Science Yield Score: compares a standard safe route with a science-weighted route pulled toward the CRISM deposits. Both routes avoid every blocked terrain cell. Each gets a Science Score (0–100) and a Safety Score (0–100), so the crew sees the trade-off between safety and science return.

Benefits and impact: the app shows hazards, oxygen limits, emergency options, and science value in one place, so a crew can plan a Marswalk that is both safe and productive. It is a planning aid for future human missions, not a flight tool.

Built with: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, and Python (rasterio, NumPy, Pillow) for the terrain processing, hosted on Vercel, with Node’s test runner for automated tests.

Creative: the point-of-no-return countdown, the mid-walk emergency reroute, and the safety-versus-science route comparison turn a static map into a decision tool.

Factors we considered: astronaut safety first. We clearly label what is real (HiRISE-derived slope hazards, Perseverance raw images) and what is simulated (telemetry, oxygen model, radiation, spectra, instrument readings, mineral percentages), and we do not claim real-world life-support or instrument accuracy.

Mars Perseverance Raw Images (live strip and waypoint photos)
